Players become junior astronauts and complete missions by answering questions about solar activity, space radiation, Mars exploration, astronaut safety and space food production. Each mission contains 10 randomly selected questions from a bank of 50, combining educational questions with fun challenges. The game provides instant feedback, explanations, points and astronaut rankings to encourage learning through play. It also connects to NASA's DONKI API to retrieve recent space-weather information, including coronal mass ejections and space-weather notifications. details:
DHRUVX is a browser-based junior astronaut training game that introduces children to space science through interactive missions.

The player begins as a junior astronaut and enters a mission after a launch countdown. Each mission contains 10 randomly selected questions from a bank of 50 questions. The questions combine educational space-science concepts with fun, child-friendly challenges. Topics include solar activity, coronal mass ejections, space radiation, Mars exploration, astronaut safety and food production in space.

After each answer, the player receives immediate feedback and a short explanation to support learning. Correct answers earn points, and the final score determines the astronaut's rank. Players can replay a mission or return to the welcome screen.

A key feature is the integration of NASA's DONKI API through a Netlify serverless function. It retrieves recent coronal mass ejection events and space-weather notifications, connecting the game to real NASA observations without exposing the API key in the browser.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Netlify was used for hosting and serverless functions. The game includes animated scenes, randomized question selection, interactive controls, score tracking and a responsive interface.

The creative approach is to combine game-based learning, child-friendly storytelling and live space-weather information in one accessible experience. DHRUVX aims to make space exploration easier to understand and inspire young learners to explore science.
